deferred_source_units.source_text: There is someone who grows rich through his attention and frugality, and this is his allotted reward:
deferred_source_units.reason: The native Proverbs 13:11 contrasts lawless acquisition with gathering in piety. It does not state Sirach's attention-and-frugality method. The distinct moral and economic descriptions are not treated as the same specific reason for growing rich.

deferred_source_units.source_text: There is someone who makes a promise to a friend because of shame, and has acquired him as an enemy for nothing.
deferred_source_units.reason: Matthew 14:7-9 says Herod promised with an oath after the dance and later acted because of the oaths and guests. It neither calls the recipient his friend nor describes her becoming his enemy through the promise, and does not say shame caused the original promise. The particular causal sequence in Sirach remains unmatched.

target_units.text: Therefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.
Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
Although the king was grieved, because of his oaths and those reclining with him, he ordered it to be given.
